What this gives a session: after Claude edits a .go, .rs, .py or .vue file, Claude Code sends the buffer to this package's `lsp.mjs` and puts what comes back into the conversation. So a layer-, scope- or licence-violating import in those languages is caught at the edit, by the same boundary table ESLint reads — instead of surviving until CI, or surviving CI, which for three of the four it does: ESLint has no parser for .go, .rs or .py, so those projects' tags have no mechanism behind them and their `lint` targets exit 0 over a violating import.

Why those four extensions and not .ts: the routed set is every extension the analyzer registry knows except the JS/TS family, and `src/lsp/editor-config.integration.test.mjs` fails if this list and that registry ever disagree. JS and TS are left out because Claude Code gives ONE server per extension — the first registered wins and the rest never start — so claiming .ts would silently displace whichever TypeScript server the developer actually needs, to re-answer a question ESLint already answers. .vue falls on the claimed side of that line even though ESLint does read it: measured, a .vue file importing a banned package draws the same @nx/enforce-module-boundaries message from both engines, so Vue is the one extension both enforcers cover.

`args` uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and `workspaceFolder` uses ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, and the two are different trees on purpose. The first is wherever this plugin was installed — inside a consumer's plugin cache, or this repository itself when a session here enables it from the tree. The second is the workspace being judged. A manifest that pointed `args` at ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} would only ever start in the one repository that contains the server, which is the whole difference between a plugin and a local script. Both variables are substituted per element as plain strings, so a path containing a quote or a backtick never reaches a shell parser.

Node must be on PATH; nothing else is installed.

Claude Code ignores manifest keys it does not know (`claude plugin validate` says so in as many words), which is where this note lives.

Bump `version` (here and in the marketplace entry, which must match — `src/conformance/plugin-catalogue.integration.test.mjs` fails when they drift) whenever THIS FILE changes: an installed plugin is cached per version, so an unbumped edit reaches nobody. Editing the server itself needs no bump when the plugin is enabled from a working tree, since `args` resolves to that tree. This version keys the manifest cache and is deliberately unrelated to the package's own version, which is what the server announces as `serverInfo`.
name: nx-polyglot-graph
description: Module-boundary diagnostics at edit time for Go, Rust, Python and Vue, from the workspace's own boundary config
